description: Server -> agent frames the Go agent must ACCEPT, and the normalised value it must act on. These defaults are load-bearing: the agent runs on the numbers it reads here, so a missing default is not a cosmetic difference but a busy loop, a dropped stream or a 0x0 terminal.

cases.why: An unconfigured agent must be useful before anyone opens settings. Every field here has to be filled by the reader: heartbeatSec 0 is a busy loop, terminalBufferBytes 0 drops every byte, gitLimit 0 shows an empty graph.

Forward compatibility in the agent's direction: a newer server sending a setting this build has never heard of is accepted and the field is dropped, so a server upgrade never strands an installed agent.
serverVersion is advisory and defaults to the empty string - a server that does not announce itself must still complete the handshake, because the version is logged, never gated on.

A browser that asks for 'a terminal' and nothing else gets a persistent session at 80x24. kind defaults to session because work must survive a dropped connection; cols/rows default because a 0x0 PTY renders nothing.

The positive control for the session-name regex: letters, digits, underscore and dash, 1..32 characters. This name is what reaches `tmux new -A -s`, so the accepted set has to stay exactly this narrow.
force defaults to false (a downgrade needs an explicit request, not an omitted field) and probationSec to 300 - the window the new binary has to complete a handshake before it rolls itself back.
